questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate cost-conscious deployment into concrete steps using Cloud Run, traffic management, and billing alerts. Covers practical, beginner-friendly use of core GCP DevOps tools without abstract theory.

## Key Concepts
- Cloud Run autoscaling knobs: concurrency, min/max instances
- Traffic splitting and revision management
- Cloud Billing budgets and alerts
- IAM basics for service, CI, and billing visibility

## Code Example
```bash
# Enable APIs
gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com

# Deploy v2 with autoscaling constraints
gcloud run deploy status-lookup-v2 \
  --image gcr.io/PROJECT/status-lookup:v2 \
  --region us-central1 \
  --platform managed \
  --concurrency 80 \
  --min-instances 0 \
  --max-instances 4

# Canary: 20% to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=20,status-lookup-v1=80

# 15 minutes later: 50/50
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=50,status-lookup-v1=50

# Final promotion: 100% to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=100

# Billing budget alert at $50/month
gcloud beta billing budgets create STATUS_LOOKUP_BUDGET --billing-account BLAHBLA --display-name "StatusLookup Budget" --amount 50 --thresholds 0.8 1.0
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate rollback if the alert triggers during a canary?
- What monitoring would you add to verify correct behavior across regions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design advanced traffic routing using header-based rules and serverless NEGs, enabling cohort-driven canaries without modifying application code paths. Emphasizes per-cohort monitoring, safe rollback procedures, and Google-native tooling integration.

## Key Concepts
- Header-based routing with URL maps and traffic weights
- Serverless NEGs and Cloud Run service management
- Per-cohort traffic distribution and rollback strategies
- Cloud Monitoring metrics and SLO evaluation
- IAM role management and Secret Manager integration

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example URL map configuration for header-based routing
name: cohort-based-url-map
defaultService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend

hostRules:
- hosts: ['*']
  pathMatcher: cohort-matcher

pathMatchers:
- name: cohort-matcher
  defaultService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
  routeRules:
  - matchRules:
    - headers:
        X-User-Cohort: A
    priority: 1
    routeAction:
      weightedBackendServices:
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v3-backend
        weight: 20
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
        weight: 80
  - matchRules:
    - headers:
        X-User-Cohort: B
    priority: 2
    routeAction:
      weightedBackendServices:
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
        weight: 100
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical implementation of Google-native deployment strategies for streaming data pipelines, specifically testing knowledge of Dataflow templates, Artifact Registry integration, Cloud Deploy canary releases, monitoring best practices, and IAM-based governance.

## Key Concepts
- Dataflow template management and versioning
- Canary deployments using Cloud Deploy traffic splitting
- Per-tenant resource governance via IAM policies
- Streaming pipeline observability and automated rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Build and publish v2 template to Artifact Registry
gcloud dataflow flex-template build "gs://my-project/templates/v2/template.json" \
  --image="us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/dataflow-templates/pipeline:v2" \
  --metadata-file="metadata.json" \
  --template-path="template.py"

# Create Cloud Deploy service and deployment
gcloud deploy apply --file=deploy.yaml
gcloud deploy releases create "v2-release" \
  --delivery-pipeline="dataflow-pipeline" \
  --region="us-central1" \
  --annotations="canary_percentage=10"
```

## Implementation Steps
1. **Build v2 Template**: Package the Dataflow template with updated logic and required dependencies
2. **Publish to Artifact Registry**: Containerize and push the template to a regional registry
3. **Configure Cloud Deploy**: Set up canary deployment with 10% traffic allocation for 15-20 minutes
4. **Traffic Splitting**: Route 10% of streaming jobs to v2 template via template parameters
5. **IAM Quotas**: Implement per-tenant quotas using custom roles and service account permissions
6. **Monitoring Setup**: Configure alerts for p95 latency (>5s), error rate (>1%), and backlog (>1000 messages)
7. **Rollback Strategy**: Pre-define rollback procedure to revert to v1 template if thresholds breached
